subject: general
question: Mohi Bahauddin Dagar, a renowned musician, is known for playing which of the following instruments?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rudra Veena.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ustad Mohi Bahauddin Dagar** is the son of renowned North Indian musician Zia Mohiuddin Dagar, he plays the Rudra veena.
 
• He performs **Dagarbani-style Rudra veena.**
 
• Referring to Nayak Haridas Dagar of the 16th century, he represents the 20th generation of the Dagar dynasty.
 
• He received the highest honour for performing artists in 2012 when the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama, presented him with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Sarangi **

 
• **A bowed stringed instrument with a resonator covered in skin is called a sarangi.**
 
• Typically, a **single block of wood** is used to handcraft a sarangi.
 
• The seventeen sympathetic strings on this instrument are constructed of steel, while the four playing strings are made of goat gut.
 
• The sarangi is a common instrument in India with numerous regional variations, but it plays a significant role in the Hindustani music of North India.
 
• The sarangi is the only musical instrument that can accurately produce all of the nuances of vocal music, including khayal, dhrupad, khayal, thumri, tappa, ghazal, and even bhajan, with embellishments and intonations.

**Sitar**

 
• **Sitar is a plucked stringed instrument, originating from the Indian subcontinent, used in Hindustani classical music.**
 
• The instrument was made of wood. It had a thin violin-type of the bridge and it was played by a plectrum worn on the right hand. It was invented by Amir Khusrau.

**Santoor **

 
• **The Santoor is a trapezoid-shaped hammered dulcimer often made of walnut wood and has 72 strings**, which are struck with two delicate carved wooden mallets.
 
• The santoor is essentially a folk instrument that originated in the Kashmir Valley, and it achieved the status of a classical instrument due to the persistent efforts and genius of Pandit Shivkumar Sharma.
 
• **Pandit Shivkumar Sharma was an Indian famous classical musician, who attained international fame by playing the musical instrument, the santoor.**
 
• With his hard work, determination and talent, Pandit Shivkumar Sharma made the santoor a global name.
